summary: Synchronous function-call schema-check service causing request queueing and 504s for enterprise customer
description: Issue summary: Enterprise customer Ledgerly reports a spike in end-to-end inference latency and an increase in 504 Gateway Timeouts for requests that include function/tool calling. Impact: multiple production endpoints returned 504s and experienced >95th percentile latencies of 2.5s+ over a 30-minute window. Initial triage suggests the extra synchronous schema-check step added by the function-call path is creating per-request remote round trips and queueing under load.
impact: Customer-facing endpoints intermittently returning 504s and high tail latency; several mission-critical pipelines delayed. Affects live customers using tool-calls with strict tail-latency requirements; billing and usage spikes observed due to retries.
environment_details: Prod cluster in us-east-1. Customer uses enterprise plan with pinned model versions and function-calling enabled. Requests travel: api-gateway -> function-proxy -> schema-validator (sync HTTP) -> serving-runtime. Schema-validator runs in shared k8s namespace (validation-service-v1).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Ledgerly test payload with function_call present (schema definition included). 2) Send 100 concurrent requests from us-east-1 over 30s. 3) Observe e2e latencies and error rate. 4) Capture traces with x-request-id. (Observed in customer and in synthetic repro harness.)
observed_behavior: Traces show a synchronous HTTP call from function-proxy to schema-validator that adds 120-380ms per request. Under concurrency, schema-validator pods experience CPU spikes and request queueing; waiting time grows non-linearly and the api-gateway begins returning 504 at the tail. Reproduced with synthetic load. Datadog trace example: https://app.datadoghq.com/trace/trace_id=abcdef123456 (private).
expected_behavior: Schema validation should not add unbounded blocking on the critical request path; tool/function-call validation should be happy-path fast or executed asynchronously without increasing e2e tail latency to cause 504s.

Full logs linked in ticket storage: s3://support-logs/ledgerly/SUP-84719/
temporary_workaround: 1) Disable function-calling for the customer's high-throughput endpoints (config toggle in console) — immediate reduction in 504s. 2) Increase schema-validator replica count and CPU for short-term mitigation. 3) Enable client-side retry jitter and backoff on Ledgerly side to reduce thundering herd.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: new sync validation integration introduced in serving-runtime v1.18 creates extra round trips.
Traces show ~150-380ms additional latency per request on validation step; when concurrent requests exceed 30, queueing in validator increases tail to >1s.
Schema-validator uses Python Flask process on shared node pool; CPU syscalls spike under validation parsing of complex nested schema (customer uses large tool schema with many properties).
A/B testing: toggling validation off for a small percentage of traffic removed the extra hop and reduced 95th percentile latency to baseline.
Related PR added a sync remote validation call rather than local schema check: infra PR #3421.
No evidence of serving-runtime model inference slowdown; problem limited to validation path and resource contention on validator pods.
Checked RBAC and network: no failed DNS or TLS handshakes observed; successful responses but delayed.
Customer reported additional retries from their client which amplified load and caused cascading queue growth.
root_cause_hypothesis: A code change introduced a synchronous remote schema-validation service call into the request path for function/tool calls. Under load the shared validator instances become CPU-bound and queue requests, causing added RTTs that drive gateway timeouts and client retries, amplifying the effect.
action_items: Hotfix: revert to local in-process schema validation path for function-call fast path (serving-runtime rollback or flag) — owner: Jonah (ENG) — PR in progress.
Mitigation: scale schema-validator replicas and increase CPU limit in us-east-1 for Ledgerly’s tenant — owner: SRE team — done (scaled x3).
Long-term: implement async validation with pessimistic fast-fail and background deep validation; add circuit-breaker around validator calls — owner: Platform/Runtime team — design ticket created.
Add validation complexity limits and server-side caching of previous schema validations per customer to reduce CPU work — owner: Runtime/Optimization team.
Add tracing and quota metrics for schema-validator latency and queue depth; alert when queue-depth > 10 for >2m — owner: Observability team.
Follow up with Ledgerly CS to review retry behavior and recommend exponential backoff changes — owner: CS team.
Post-incident: produce a short postmortem and update function-call runbook — owner: Support Lead.
Test surface: add load test with large schema payloads in CI to detect regressions early — owner: QA.
Schedule: hotfix rollout targeted for 2026-03-13 07:00 UTC; full async redesign Q2 roadmap item.
resolution: Work in progress. Temporary mitigations applied: validation scaled and customer advised to disable function-calling for high-throughput endpoints. Hotfix PR to revert to local validation submitted and under review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/210. Customer notified and monitoring shows error rate trending down after mitigation.
